here = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(__file__))
topsrcdir = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(here)))
topcommdir = os.path.join(topsrcdir, "comm")
DOC_ROOT = os.path.join(topcommdir, "docs")

with open(os.path.join(DOC_ROOT, "config.yml"), "r") as fh:
        docs_config = yaml.safe_load(fh)

    if not disable_fatal_errors and "allowed_errors" in docs_config:
        fatal_errors = _check_sphinx_errors(warnings, docs_config)

# Note: doc_trees does not include the "comm/" prefix to paths
# Note: In order for CI to pick up the need to rebuild docs, documentation
#  paths must include a "docs/" directory.
doc_trees:
    adr: docs/adr
    addrbook: mail/components/addrbook/docs
    backend: mailnews/base/docs
    build: docs/build
    calendar: calendar/docs
    cxx: docs/cxx
    documentation: docs/docs
    exchange: mailnews/protocols/exchange/docs
    frontend: mail/base/docs
    inappnotifications: mail/components/inappnotifications/docs
    l10n: docs/l10n
    mots: docs/mots
    panorama: mailnews/db/panorama/docs
    rust: rust/docs
    storybook: mail/components/storybook/docs
    telemetry: docs/telemetry
    testing: docs/testing

text: The docs command repair sets DOC_ROOT under topcommdir and reads config.yml there instead of the Gecko docs root. Accepted docs/config.yml maps topic names to component docs trees without a comm/ prefix. Keep this checkout boundary in Thunderbird documentation tooling; changing topsrcdir or copying a Gecko command can silently select the wrong config. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Build Thunderbird docs from the comm docs root
